134.history: A settlement on the western coast where the boars ran heaviest in the thickets. Its settlers hung boar tusks over their doors and took boar for their chief meat for the rest of the age, and the island came to know a man of that place by his gait, from a lifetime of walking ground a boar might break from underfoot. Its households kept the sharing before the storms by bringing boar meat salted in the Red Hill's salt, and it was said at the ford that no settlement of the west brought fatter shares or quarrelled longer over the weighing of them.

282.history: A harbour on the west coast beside a stone landing built by hands none of its settlers could name, older than any wall near it. Households took it up in the two thousand six hundred and seventieth year and used the landing as they found it rather than mend it, out of the caution settlers kept wherever the Old Ones' work still stood; the harbour was fully settled by the two thousand seven hundred and fifty-fifth year and shipped the western grain along the coast.

255.history: A banked hill-fort in the midst of the island, between the Red Hill and the hills of the vein. Herders wanting the bank to face south and quarrymen wanting it to face north raised a single crooked earthwork that answered both wants at once and satisfied neither, and the fort stood from its first year with a name that fitted it more ways than its builders meant. Its holder Ruadhan Beag quarrelled two winters with the holder of Dùn thais over which way a bank ought to face, until Murchadh rode to hear them and left the ditch as it stood, finding a hundred years without an enemy a better argument than either holder made.
255.known_for: the bank that faced two ways

23.history: Households settled on the ground below a broken watch-tower of the Old Ones in the two thousand eight hundred and forty-seventh year and asked Eithne nic Ailein, then a hundred and forty-four years old, to lay out their fields; she stayed. Her households named the place Cathair mhòr, the great city, out of hope rather than size, and took no stone from the ruin above them though it was the nearest quarry. Eithne's knot-keeper walked at the head of her household with its cord about his arm when she came down to the valley below Dùn ìseal in the last years.
23.known_for: Eithne's fields below the ruined tower

318.history: A hill south of the valleys already called, by no teller then living able to say why, the holy hill. Households came to it for its spring in the two thousand eight hundred and seventieth year and settled it in earnest a generation later, keeping its water and the fact of its holiness together without asking more of either. The households cut the spring's channel no deeper than they found it, and lit no fire within sight of the source. In the great gathering of the three thousandth year they sent water from the holy spring to the ford in sealed pots, and it was poured into the river at dusk.
318.known_for: the spring of the holy hill

326.history: A settlement near the south coast between the beacon at Tobar dhearg and the old Seann Skell, whose first houses stood on driven piles over standing marsh water. They were moved to firm ground a bowshot inland once the piles had proved the footing sound, and kept the name the marsh first gave them. It was founded in earnest in the two thousand nine hundred and eighty-sixth year and traded with the fishers of the strait at Caol ruadh. The marsh gave the settlers eels and wildfowl in plenty, and the moving of the houses to firm ground was done over three summers, one row at a time, so that no household was ever without a roof while it was done.
326.known_for: the houses on piles over the marsh

246.history: A hill above the upper reaches of the rivers where, in the three thousand one hundred and third year, the kin of a settling household's head carried stones up the slope above the cattle-fold and raised the first cairn there, one stone laid at a time by whoever had known him. Within a lifetime the slope held as many small heaps of stone as the fold below held cattle in a good year. The households settled the hill fully in the three thousand two hundred and eighteenth year, round the cattle-fold.
